newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine government bemoans labor reform delays.
newsitem.headline: Argentine government bemoans labor reform delays.

text.p: The Argentine government complained on Monday that delays in the Congress in passing a labor reform bill are discouraging companies from hiring new staff.
"The fact that the new way of hiring personnel is not yet approved paralizes the hiring of workers," Secretary for Economic Planning Eugenio Pendas told reporters.
"While waiting for a definition of the labor reform bill, employers prefer that their workers do overtime," he said.

Months ago the government sent to Congress a labor reform package designed to reduce 17.1 percent unemployment by easing the burden for employers of redundancy payments, making working hours more flexible and reducing payroll taxes.

The government, which has a majority both in the Senate and the lower house, expected quick approval. But the bill, endorsed by businessmen, has faced strong resistance from unions and their allies in Congress.
